# Return-Target Feasibility Analysis

*Generated by `research/analysis/return_target_feasibility.py`. Seed 20260826, 20,000 paths, 5-year horizon, 365 trading days/year.*

This file is generated. Do not edit by hand; re-run the script.

## 1. The compounding ceiling

For a strategy with true Sharpe `S` run at annualised volatility `sigma`,
expected log growth is `g = S*sigma - sigma^2/2`, maximised at `sigma = S`.
So the **maximum CAGR attainable at any leverage** is `exp(S^2/2) - 1`.
Leverage past that point lowers compound growth while still raising drawdown.

| True Sharpe | Max CAGR (full Kelly) | Vol at full Kelly | CAGR at 1/2 Kelly | CAGR at 1/4 Kelly |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.3 | 4.6% | 30.0% | 3.4% | 2.0% |
| 0.5 | 13.3% | 50.0% | 9.8% | 5.6% |
| 0.7 | 27.8% | 70.0% | 20.2% | 11.3% |
| 0.8 | 37.7% | 80.0% | 27.1% | 15.0% |
| 1.0 | 64.9% | 100.0% | 45.5% | 24.5% |
| 1.2 | 105.4% | 120.0% | 71.6% | 37.0% |
| 1.5 | 208.0% | 150.0% | 132.5% | 63.6% |
| 2.0 | 638.9% | 200.0% | 348.2% | 139.9% |
| 2.5 | 2176.0% | 250.0% | 942.0% | 292.4% |

**Sharpe required to reach the target band:**

| Target CAGR | Full Kelly | 1/2 Kelly | 1/4 Kelly |
|---|---|---|---|
| 60.0% | 0.97 | 1.12 | 1.47 |
| 65.0% | 1.00 | 1.16 | 1.51 |
| 75.0% | 1.06 | 1.22 | 1.60 |
| 100.0% | 1.18 | 1.36 | 1.78 |

## 2. The drawdown attached to the target

Each row is levered to the volatility that produces roughly the target CAGR
for that Sharpe. `student_t` uses Student-t(4) innovations; `garch` adds
GARCH(1,1) volatility clustering (alpha=0.09, beta=0.90) on top.

## 3. Could we even detect the required Sharpe?

Standard error of an annualised Sharpe estimate, by sample length
(iid assumption -- the true SE is larger under autocorrelation and negative skew):

| True Sharpe | 2y SE | 3y SE | 5y SE | 8y SE | 95% CI on a 5y estimate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 | 0.75 | 0.61 | 0.47 | 0.38 | [-0.43, 1.43] |
| 1.0 | 0.87 | 0.71 | 0.55 | 0.43 | [-0.07, 2.07] |
| 1.2 | 0.93 | 0.76 | 0.59 | 0.46 | [0.05, 2.35] |
| 1.5 | 1.03 | 0.84 | 0.65 | 0.52 | [0.22, 2.78] |
| 2.0 | 1.22 | 1.00 | 0.77 | 0.61 | [0.48, 3.52] |

**Expected best in-sample Sharpe from a search over worthless strategies.**
This is what a search with *zero* real edge is expected to hand us, purely
from selecting the maximum of N noisy estimates. Any backtest Sharpe below
the relevant cell is evidence of nothing.
